Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 966756
Permit API: 117-22124
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 9/02/2022
Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-015 collected on 8/10/2022 at 14:00 as part of inspection report #3405181 at the Repsol Johnson (02-135) Well Site. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-015 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Barium - 122 ug/L; Strontium- 7.21 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- 4,900 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 904.1 mg/L. (Photo 1)Repsol submitted a 15 day response to NOV #406500 on August 30, 2022. According to the response letter, Resource Environmental was engaged to conduct site characterization work for an unknown volume of 'suspected produced water' spilled to the stormwater, soils, and gravels of the Johnson Pad. On August 11, 2022, Resource Environmental conducted screening surveys of stormwater pools and measured Electrical Conductivity readings of between 1.61 and 7.14 mS/cm on the pad surface. Additional characterization took place on August 12, 2022 through the collection of soil samples. Resource Environmental will conduct followup screenings and further site delineation is scheduled for September 6, 2022 following the removal of mobile tanks from the impacted area. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/16/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 5/16/2023 at 0902 hours. The weather was 56 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to follow-up on remedial activities occurring onsite related to a release from 4/6/2023.Sumps constructed as part of the remedial efforts in the excavated/impacted areas remain in place and continue to have collected fluids recovered. All excavated areas remain exposed and were mostly dry today. The southern stormwater conveyance channel that was impacted as a result of the release from 4/6/2023 remains excavated (photos #2 and 3). The impacted stormwater control basin was empty and dry today (photo #4). Impacted material excavated as a result of the release remains staged onsite. Portions of the impacted material are held within lined residual waste containers on secondary containment and portions are held directly on secondary containment and covered with liner. The residual waste containers are in the process of being trucked offsite. Pooled water held within the impacted/excavated area located just west of the initial release point (photo #7) was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at ~900us/cm today. Water held in the northern stormwater conveyance channel was field measured for EC at ~700us/cm today (photo #5). Discussion to excavate further along the produced water flow-line as explained in inspection record #3543714 has been completed and soil characterization samples have been collected. Violations cited against API #015-23733 on 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are noted at this time. I departed the site at 1030 hours.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 906090
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2021
Comments: On January 27, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up to spill notification 354567 at Beech Resources Premier Pad. During the rig down process after the stimulation of the new wells was completed, Don Stevenson of Beech Resources reported areas of elevated conductivity around the MASS onsite. DEP met with Don Stevenson and he showed the DEP where the brine water spill occurred. Areas with the highest conductivity were found at each of the off loading sites and were excavated. The path around the MASS was also scraped up to removed the impacted stone where the trucks tires tracked the brine water around the MASS. The amount of the spill was estimated at about 70 gallons. Penn E&R is scheduled to complete the site characterization. Beech Resources plans to begin the ACT 2 process. The DEP recommends addressing the operation of the off loading of brine water to a MASS to avoid having these types of spills. This spill is a violation of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, an on-site meeting was held at the operator's request at the former location of the MAWC well pad in Springfield Township, Fayette County. The purpose of this meeting was to assess current vegetative growth and review areas lacking 70% vegetative growth coverage. This also a follow-up inspection to IR 4178423. A Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) was executed between the Department and the operator on December 16, 2021. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed during the inspection:The former well site appears to have overall established additional vegetative growth since the time of IR 4175984; exhibiting approximately 50% vegetative growth during this inspection. The temporary stabilization applied on site appears to be adequate at the time of inspection. Additional reportedly third-party vehicle tracks were observed at the former well pad location (photos 3, 5, and 10). Daugherty reported that the landowner installed signs at the site entrance that prohibit vehicular use on site (photo 14). The Department recommends that the operator continue to document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, take reasonable efforts to stop them while promoting continued vegetative growth, and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site.The super silt fence remains installed at the northern boundary of the former well site (photo 13). Daugherty reported that it is to remain installed as during site restoration as an Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control measure. It appears that the portion of it located within the site boundaries have been repaired and maintained in accordance with current regulations. The Department recommended during this inspection that the operator continue to maintain the super silt fence in accordance with manufacturer specifications, if it is to remain in-use during site restoration.No loose sediment was observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap that reportedly pre-exists well site construction (photo 11).Minor areas that appear to be susceptible to receiving high winds and concentrated stormwater flow were identified on site during this inspection. The Department recommended during this inspection that the operator consider additional E and S control measures to prevent potential displacement of mulch and seed, such as erosion control blanketing.While leaving site, the Department observed that Daugherty had started work on site with an overseeder.Based on observations from this inspection, the violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding.

Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: On April 24, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. According to the incident report that was submitted by the operator, this spill occurred on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM and resulted in an estimated 50 barrel release of production fluids to the ground. This spill report was received by the Department at 2:16 PM.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who explained that the brine tank valve failed and was ejected from the brine tank, which resulted in the release of an estimated 50 barrels of a brine and crude oil mixture. This was quantified based on the most recent fluid level measurement taken on the brine tank. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth are reported to have occurred. Penneco representative John Dohman was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Dohman who confirmed that no impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth have resulted from this incident. No identifiable water resources were visible from the location of the release. Mr. Dohman estimated that the release traveled approximately 70 yards down the slope adjacent to the brine tank and was stopped by a fallen tree. He explained that absorbent material was placed on the impacted area to absorb any standing production fluids and oil absorbent booms were placed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the release. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/06/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8178831
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/06/2024
Comments: On 3/6/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 49 degrees, overcast and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Carlos Martinez who described current operations as follows: The Patterson 805 drilling rig is set up on site drilling surface and intermediate on five new wells. The rig finished drilling surface and intermediate on all five wells. They were currently drilling the production on the 109HU, in the process of drilling the tangent with the curve and lateral to follow. Carlos expects this rig to drill to TD and run casing and cement before being towered down and removed from location. Patterson 801 will drill production on the other four wells.Carlos accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were three frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did discover a channel of water along the north perimeter berm that appeared to have a white substance in it. The water field tested at 4.10 mS conductance. The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. I did witness the white substance along the length of the water puddle. I did witness a 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. Sample 9551087 was collected from the water puddle on the pad surface. The water puddle on the pad extended east another 30' past a transformer. Water east of the transformer field tested at 2.29 mS conductance.Visible from the pad surface, I did witness a white plume leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. Sample 9551088 was collected from where the water was entering into the sediment basin. Water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. I did witness emerging vegetation in the constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and entering the sediment basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface and sediment basin. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad; clean/report as necessary.2. Determine the cause of elevated conductance fluid and of the white substance and prevent a reoccurrence.3. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1530 hours.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 2/24/2026 to OIL & GAS MGMT INC in Addison Township, Somerset county. 78.88(a) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to inspect each operating well quarterly for compliance with the well construction and operating requirements.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 2/24/2026
Violation Code: 78.88(a) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to inspect each operating well quarterly for compliance with the well construction and operating requirements.
Violation ID: 8265965
Permit API: 111-20249
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Addison Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/24/2026
Comments: On 2/24/26 at 9:11 AM, I arrived at the Walker 1616 OG Well to conduct a Routine/Complete Inspection. At the time of the inspection all the valves on the well tree were shut (Photograph #4). The well appears to not be producing based on the valve alignment and absence of chart in the meter box. (Photograph #17) A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator had not submitted the Annual Production Report for 2025. Violations 78.121(A) and 78.121(B) are being cited for failure to submit annual production. A check of DEP records on 2/24/26 found that the operator has not submitted the Mechanical Integrity Assessment report for 2025. Violations 78.88(e), 78.88(b)1-4 and 78.88(d) are being cited for failure to submit integrity report. The operators posting is attached to the well tree. (Photograph #1) Using a Bascom Turner 611, calibrated on 2/13/26, no gas was detected around the well tree. (Photographs 6-16). The separators have surface corrosion but no signs of leaks, spills or equipment failure were noticed. No gas was detected around the equipment using the Bascom Turner 611. The production tank appears to be in sound condition, no signs of leaks or damage were found. The production tank is not attached to the production equipment. DEP recommend the tank be removed if it is no longer in use. Attached to the meter box is a former operator's posting. The sticker should be removed since it displays incorrect information as to the operator of the well. (Photograph #17)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/25/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/25/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 966152
Permit API: 081-21882
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/25/2022
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions after multiple spills occurred on Pad B since fracing began on the pad early in the year. I met with EQT company man Justin Hamill upon arriving on Pad B. Nine wells have been drilled on Pad B but not all of the wells have been completed. Equipment from the frac has been removed from the pad. Most of the well site secondary containment has been removed from the pad. The secondary containment remains in the southeast area of the pad. The southeast corner of the containment was pulled back somewhat during this inspection and revealed fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) from 4.32 to 3.10 mS/cm which had been beneath the containment. A puddle with an EC of 3.00 mS/cm was also observed on the pad surface south of the sump installed in the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid in the sump was 1.4 mS/cm. The stormwater channel appeared dry.On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding.

Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/08/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8182726
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/08/2024
Comments: On April 8, 2024, inspection conducted on the Tutelo 2 well in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred the day prior to this inspection at 7:00 PM, and was reported to the Department that same evening at approximately 9:00 PM by Penneco representative Marc Jacobs (see attached Spill Report). The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Jacobs while en route to the well site, who explained that a dry-rotted high-pressure hose connected to the well ruptured and released from 1 to 2 barrels of oil onsite. He subsequently explained that Penneco representatives were working nearby when they heard the hose rupture and were able to initiate a prompt response. Present with the Department during this inspection were Woodard and Curran consultants Matt Kapral and Clayton Hefner. Additional representatives from Penneco and Woodard and Curran were also onsite.This inspection report is part 1 of 2, covering the Department's inspection in response to this incident.The following was observed:The access road to the well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). This access road is shared with the Tutelo 1 (129-23915) well site. Materials were staged along the access road for installation of CFS (see photo 2). An unnamed stream or tributary was observed approximately 150 feet south of the well site that flows through a culvert underneath the access road. An oil absorbent boom was observed in this location (see photo 3). The Department spoke with Mr. Kapral and Mr. Hefner who explained that seven additional oil absorbent booms were placed across the unnamed stream or tributary downslope of the cross-culvert under the access road. They further explained that a sheen was observed where the first oil absorbent boom was placed upstream from the access road culvert. Peatmoss was spread on impacted areas not yet excavated onsite (see photos 5 and 6). Brush clearing was conducted on the slope east of the well site to remove impacted vegetation and prepare for excavation of impacted soil (see photos 7 and 8). Minor excavation work had been conducted upon arrival to site to contain impacted material, according to onsite representatives (see photos 9 and 18). Additional excavations were conducted while the Department was onsite. Onsite brine tanks appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 10). A large tarp was laid west of well site for placement of excavated impacted material (see photo 11). Heavy oil staining was observed on the ground around the well head upon arrival to site (see photo 14). It was equipped with a well tag, and the operator's information was posted on the separator (see photos 16 and 17). The aforementioned sheen was observed upstream of the access road culvert, with fluid beading on the wet rocks in this location (see photos 19 and 20). Due to observations made in this location, the Department subsequently collected water samples in this location. While the Department sampled, CFS installations were conducted (see photos 21 and 22). The overall size of the impacted ground area appeared to be approximately 100 feet by 100 feet at the well site, with approximately 100 additional feet of the access road also being impacted. An oil odor was detectable within an approximate 150 foot radius of the well site. Based on observations from this inspection, remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2 is recommended. Violations are being issued in response to observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt of analytical results from samples collected during this inspection. Please see IR 3742855 for inspection report documenting the Department's collection of aqueous samples from the onsite unnamed stream or tributary.

Comments: Routine site inspection on November 14, 2023 with Evan Buck of DEP. During our inspection we inspected both the well pad and freshwater impoundment (FWI). The operator was issued a new ESCGP3 (ESG291421001-00) in April 2021 which incorporates storm water features and a slight well pad reduction. To date, these new features in the ESCGP3 haven't been completed. The well pad remains at full built-out size with gravel throughout the well pad. The FWI remains intact with >8ft. freeboard. No E and S issues were observed. Both the well pad and FWI appear stable.There are 3 producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. Well cellars have been backfilled with gravel. There are three gas production units (GPUs) onsite. Gas from each GPU is metered before discharging into Superior Appalachian's 8" steel pipeline. There are (3) 400 BBL produced fluids tanks stationed on the well pad in a modular secondary containment. The Department recommends labeling the produced fluids tanks. Approximately 4" of water was observed in the secondary containment system with a conductivity reading of 390 uS/cm. Rust was observed on the exterior or the produced fluids tanks. The Department recommends monitoring the tanks and repainting or replacing the tanks if needed. A skid mounted compressor unit is located onsite. Stained gravel was observed near the skid mounted compressor unit (pictures 4-7). The stained gravel extends the entire length of the compressor unit and several feet away from the unit. Visible drips on the gravel were observed which appear to be coolant and oil. Two different oil mats were laying near the compressor unit, saturated in oil. One on the front side and one on the back side of the unit. I observed similar oil stains in my April 24, 2023 inspection (3536704). A drum of coolant was observed near the compressor unit not in secondary containment. The Department recommends that all drums be labeled and placed in secondary containment. During the inspection, I reached out to Bob Liddle of LPR and told Mr. Liddle of our findings. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown amount of oil and coolant released to the ground, the Department encourages the operator to pursue the Act 2 process for site remediation.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2024
Comments: On November 6, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Beech Resources reported a spill of approximately 210 barrels of produced fluid on the evening of November 5, 2024. Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. Mr. Stevenson said that a coupler failed on a freshwater pump connected to a Y fitting that blended with production fluid. When the failure happened the production fluid pump overtook the line and released the production fluid onto the well pad surface. The pad is being used as a staging area for the Delta Well Pad stimulation so there was already equipment onsite. Immediately, a vacuum truck began removing the free liquid off the well pad surface. Approximately half of the well pad surface was impacted by produced fluid spill. Beech Resources and their contractors worked through the night of November 5, 2024 to excavate and remove about 90 percent of the impacted surface. During the inspection, Penn E and R arrived onsite to screen the excavation for further impacted areas and collect Act 2 confirmatory samples. DEP broadly screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter and the range of conductivity in the excavation was 200 uS/cm to 2,000 uS/cm. Beech Resources plans to move the impacted soil into dumpsters and have it hauled off site. DEP did not observe any indication of the produced fluid leaving the well pad. Due to the production fluid spill onto the well pad surface violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. Beech Resources plans to remediate the site through the Act 2 process.

DEP broadly screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter and the range of conductivity in the excavation was 200 uS/cm to 2,000 uS/cm. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/05/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/05/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8248040
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

No sediment was observed in the stormwater culvert where the roadside ditch empties (photos 3 and 4). The ground was scoured by stormwater on eastern side of the access road (photo 5). The Department followed this scouring up the access road to a deep accelerated erosion rill adjacent to the well pad (photo 6). This deep accelerated erosion rill appears to be the source of the scouring and sedimentation shown in Photos in 2-5, due to the potential for channelized stormwater flow.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the overtopped CFS and the accelerated erosion and sedimentation in the access road.

Comments: I performed an INCDT inspection upon notice of a release of produced water reported to the Department on the Abbott Pad. The weather at the time of inspection was overcast and about 31 degrees F. According to the spill notice, CID#338740, Steve Watson (Cabot Oil & Gas) notified DEP Answering Service who contacted Jonathan Ulanoski (NERO - ER). Jonathan notified Mike O'Donnell (Scranton Office - O&G) that on 12/12/18 Tetra (water transfer contractor) was disconnecting a section of the transfer line on the tank pad. While doing so, approximately 1-2 bbls of residual frac fluid from the line spilled off containment onto the tank pad surface. The spill was reported to the Department within the 2-hour reporting requirement at 5:50 pm. It was reported that at the time of the notification the spill area had been coned off, covered with plastic, and secured for the night. On 12/13/2018 remediation efforts were to be put into place. Resource Environmental will be overseeing all remediation activities. On 12/13/2018, I met with Abby Vogler and Christian Mondy from Resource Environmental. Prior to excavating the area impacted by the release, it was noted that the highest recorded conductivity at any of the screened sampling points was found to be 0.446 millisiemens. After excavation the highest reading in the affected area was 0.148 millisiemens . The excavation (Photo 4) was about 2-4 inches deep in an area about 25' x 25'. There were approximately 3-4 yards of pad material excavated into a rolloff container (Photo 5). I spoke with Herb Swiney, Contract Safety Consultant,on site as well, who stated the site was secured immediately after the release and a rolloff container was called for. The container was to arrive the following morning, 12/13/2018, and excavation started upon arrival. The site was reportedly covered overnight and due to the freezing conditions, the release stayed mostly surficial. By phone, I then spoke with Steve Watson, Cabot representative. He indicated that systematic random sampling for Act 2 would occur this afternoon, (December 13, 2018). The rolloff container would either go to Alliance or Keystone landfill. A report will be prepared detailing the sampling results. While onsite, I also performed a RTNC E&S inspection. The access road (Photo 7) and pad surfaces were solid and stable, as was the cut and fill slopes of the tank and well pads (Photos 6 and 8). The vegetation was visible through the snow and appeared to meet stabilization requirements. There were no erosional anomalies noted during the inspection. There are violations attached to this inspection.
